headline: Mushfiqur out as Tigers face West Indies in first Test
summary: Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto won the toss and elected to bat first in Mirpur, but veteran Mushfiqur Rahim was ruled out due to a hand injury.
details: Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto won the toss and elected to bat first against the West Indies in the opening Test of the two-match series at the Sher-e-Bangla National cricket stadium in Mirpur.
Veteran batter Mushfiqur Rahim was ruled out of the match after sustaining a hand injury during training, with Towhid Hridoy replacing him in the playing XI.

Shoriful Islam also joined the lineup, replacing Ebadot Hossain. The Tigers retained all three spinners from their recent match against Afghanistan: Mehidy Hasan Miraz, Nayeem Hasan, and Taijul Islam.
The team is looking to bounce back after a disappointing tour of the UAE, including a frustrating draw against Afghanistan and losses in the ODI tri-series against Zimbabwe and Afghanistan.
Motivation is high as Bangladesh currently sits fourth in the World Test Championship (WTC) standings. Reaching the WTC final at The Oval in June could be a major milestone.
To keep their hopes of reaching the final alive, the Tigers will need to win at least four of their remaining six Tests and draw another.
caption:

The team is looking to bounce back after a disappointing tour of the UAE, including a frustrating draw against Afghanistan and losses in the ODI tri-series against Zimbabwe and Afghanistan.

Motivation is high as Bangladesh currently sits fourth in the World Test Championship (WTC) standings. Reaching the WTC final at The Oval in June could be a major milestone.

headline: Medical tests for Malaysia-bound workers to begin Oct 31
summary: The Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare warns that any medical exams conducted before this date will not be accepted for immigration clearance.
details: Bangladeshi nationals wishing to work in Malaysia will be able to begin getting medical examinations at approved medical centres from Saturday, October 31.

The Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare warned that eligible candidates will not be able to get medical examinations before this date, and any tests conducted earlier will not be accepted for immigration clearance.
A list of approved medical centres will be published on the ministry's website soon. The ministry noted that centres may be added or removed based on their capacity and compliance with instructions.
The government has warned workers against brokers and unscrupulous agencies offering unauthorized medical tests in exchange for money and passports.
To obtain BMET clearance, agencies must submit relevant documents and Visa with Reference (VDR) documents to the approved medical centres.
Medical centres that fail to comply with ministry instructions face closure, and the recruitment activities of associated agencies may be suspended.
On October 22, the government announced that Malaysia had agreed in principle to take in 10,000 Bangladeshi workers completely free of charge, with 338 recruiting agencies listed for the process.
caption:
Planning to work in Malaysia? Medical tests start October 31—any tests done before this date will be rejected.

Bangladeshi nationals wishing to work in Malaysia will be able to begin getting medical examinations at approved medical centres from Saturday, October 31.

The Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare warned that eligible candidates will not be able to get medical examinations before this date, and any tests conducted earlier will not be accepted for immigration clearance.

A list of approved medical centres will be published on the ministry's website soon. The ministry noted that centres may be added or removed based on their capacity and compliance with instructions.

The government has warned workers against brokers and unscrupulous agencies offering unauthorized medical tests in exchange for money and passports.

To obtain BMET clearance, agencies must submit relevant documents and Visa with Reference (VDR) documents to the approved medical centres.

Medical centres that fail to comply with ministry instructions face closure, and the recruitment activities of associated agencies may be suspended.

On October 22, the government announced that Malaysia had agreed in principle to take in 10,000 Bangladeshi workers completely free of charge, with 338 recruiting agencies listed for the process.
